beats: Your washer makes you wait before the door opens. Some don't.
Most washer doors are locked by a tiny heater, not a motor.
Inside the lock, a small ceramic pill heats up when the cycle starts.
Against it sits a disc made of two metals bonded together.
One metal stretches more with heat, so the warm disc suddenly snaps the other way.
That snap pushes a pin into the door's hook. Locked.
The same move closes a switch, so the machine can fill and spin.
At the end, the heater stops, but the disc needs a minute or two to cool.
Only then does it snap back and pull the pin out.
Even in a power cut mid-spin, the heat keeps the door shut while the drum slows.
If yours opens instantly with a click, that's an electromagnet, and the machine checks the drum first.
So that wait isn't a fault. It's a tiny heater cooling down.
